evals.prompt: Add per-user rate limiting to our Express API: 100 requests per minute per API key, return 429 with a Retry-After header, keep the counters in the Redis client we already use, and make sure the existing tests still pass.
evals.expected_output: A recon-backed plan in .orchestrator/ with testable acceptance criteria, concrete examples, frozen contracts, a pre-mortem, task briefs with write-sets, oracles and Verify blocks, then a short summary and a stop for approval before any code is written.
expectations: Creates a feature branch and runs orch.sh init before planning
Fills PLAN 'Verify (global)' and 'Verify (per task)', then runs orch.sh baseline
Dispatches orch-scout with model haiku rather than the built-in Explore or a fork
PLAN.md lists acceptance criteria for the 429 status, the Retry-After header, and the per-key limit
PLAN.md has an Examples table in plain words and a plain-language summary
PLAN.md reuses the existing Redis client instead of planning a new one
Every brief has Risk and Oracle in its header, a Write-set with test: entries, named test cases, and a fenced Verify block with one command per line
Sets STATE status to awaiting-approval and shows the user at most 20 lines, asking them to confirm the examples, before dispatching any executor

evals.expected_output: Follows the Resume protocol: reads state and git, gates in-progress tasks, never re-dispatches finished ones, and continues from NEXT ACTION.
expectations: Runs orch.sh status and reads .orchestrator/STATE.md before doing anything else
Does not re-dispatch any task marked [x]
For each [~] task, runs orch.sh gate <ID> before deciding to re-dispatch
A re-dispatch goes through orch.sh dispatch <ID>, whose prompt carries the partial-work line
Updates the updated: field with the current tool and model

evals.prompt: Use the orchestrate skill to fix the typo 'recieve' in the error message in src/errors.ts.
evals.expected_output: Sized as XS: the orchestrator makes the one-line fix itself, runs the relevant tests and orch.sh quick, and reports, without subagents or an .orchestrator/ directory.
expectations: No subagent is dispatched
No .orchestrator/ directory is created
Only src/errors.ts changes (plus any test that asserts the message)
Relevant tests are run and orch.sh quick passes before reporting

evals.prompt: Orchestrate this, go as fast as you can, run everything in parallel: add three new REST endpoints (GET /reports, POST /reports, DELETE /reports/:id), each with tests.
evals.expected_output: Applies the parallel-safety checks instead of fanning out blindly: the shared route registry and shared types become an early serialized task, and parallel writers run only if every check passes, each in its own worktree.
expectations: Reads references/parallelism.md before choosing a wave layout
Assigns the route registry (or equivalent hot file) to exactly one task
Shared request and response types are defined as a contract in PLAN before any fan-out
Any parallel wave goes through orch.sh dispatch --worktree with at most 3 tasks, each dispatched with isolation worktree
Each worktree task is gated with its directory and merged with orch.sh merge
Logs the parallel-or-sequential decision in LEDGER.md

evals.prompt: I'm not a developer. On our billing app, customers should see invoice amounts in their own currency instead of always USD. Can you just get this done?
evals.expected_output: Treats the requester as a product owner: plain-language summary, concrete before/after examples to confirm (including what must not change), a high risk tier because billing is touched, and a clear statement that a code owner must approve the PR.
expectations: Asks the requester to confirm concrete examples written in their terms, including at least one example that must not change
PLAN 'Release and approval' marks the risk tier high and names code-owner approval
Does not skip the approval stop even though the requester asked to just get it done, because billing is high risk
The final report leads with what changed for users and how to undo it, before any technical detail
Never pushes or opens a PR without asking

evals.expected_output: The .orchestrator/STATE.md present belongs to another branch (its branch: line differs from the current branch). The orchestrator reports it as a foreign run and does not resume it.
expectations: Runs orch.sh status first and notices FOREIGN RUN
Does not dispatch, gate, or edit anything belonging to the foreign run
Tells the user whose run it is (branch and owner) and offers to start a new run instead

evals.prompt: Orchestrate: add an endpoint that lets a logged-in user delete their own account and all their data.
evals.expected_output: High-risk handling end to end: plan review by orch-reviewer on opus, tasks marked high risk, every high-risk gate followed by a task review and orch.sh review, object-level authorization tests, and a report that names the code-owner approval.
expectations: Dispatches orch-reviewer with Mode: plan before asking for approval
Briefs touching auth or data deletion carry Risk: high
After a gate exits 4, dispatches orch-reviewer Mode: task and then runs orch.sh review
Test cases include a user trying to delete another user's account and being refused
The report states that a code owner must approve the PR
